correctness.rationale: Two independently encoded, exhaustive state-generation methods cover all 3108 matchings: least-uncovered-vertex edge-mask recursion, and 12-to-12 bipartite assignment with nibble-encoded mates. Both enumerate 24 embedded face swaps from scratch, verify 9048 undirected edges and 15 flux-homogeneous components, and BFS from every state, with all 15 componentwise and all 163 nonzero distance-bin counts matching exactly. The standalone programs reproduce the total within-sector unordered-distance sum 10,795,608. The finite domain and every state/neighbor/distance are checked; no claim for infinitely many torus sizes is made. Retaining the exact scripts and JSON certificate allows reconstruction without external dependencies. Risks: implementation correlation and absence of independent formal audit.

value.rationale: A 24-cell anisotropic square torus is a minimal, geometrically natural bipartite torus beyond the 4-by-4 illustrative case in the toroidal-domino literature. The complete 15-sector combinatorial metric data quantify freezing (four isolates), minimal mobility (four 24-cycles), flux-dependent traversal radius and 20-step maximum diameter, and all-pair distances for a 1,456-state mobile sector. These aggregate invariants directly distinguish flexibility and reconfiguration bottlenecks invisible in a plain total matching count or component lower bound. The precise sector census is a plausible benchmark for topological/height-function counting methods and local Markov-chain geometry; no unwarranted general theorem or physical mixing result is inferred.
